of a 25 year old female with fever"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is the case of a 25-year-old female, a resident of Nalgonda, and a homemaker, who presented to the outpatient department \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Ethree days ago\u003C\/span\u003E with chief complaints of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Generalised body pains since 9 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Bilateral knee ankle, metacarpophalangeal joint pains since 9 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Fever since 6 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Headache since 6 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHistory of presenting Illness\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003E9\u0026nbsp;days ago \u003C\/span\u003Ewhen she developed \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Egeneralised body aches\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Ewhich were sudden in onset, continuous, aggravated with the onset of fever and relieved on taking medication.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003E9 days ago, \u003C\/span\u003Ethe patient also had \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Ejoint pains \u003C\/span\u003Ewhich were present bilaterally in the knee joints, the metacarpophalangeal joints, and the ankle joints. The Joint pains were of dull character, sudden in onset, continuous,\u0026nbsp; did not cause any functional impairment, and aggravated on the onset of fever.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003E6 days ago\u003C\/span\u003E, the patient developed a sudden onset, \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Ehigh-grade fever,\u003C\/span\u003E \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Eassociated with chills and rigour. \u003C\/span\u003EAccording to the patient, the fever was in the range of 101-104 degrees Fahrenheit as measured on separate occasions, it was continuous with no diurnal variation (the patient denies any fever-free intervals during the day). The fever was relieved with medication.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWith the onset of fever \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003E6 days ago\u003C\/span\u003E, the patient also developed a \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Eheadache\u003C\/span\u003E which was sudden in onset, diffuse, throbbing in character, and continuous. It aggravated on rise in body temperature and was relieved on taking medication.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe headache was not associated with nausea, vomiting, retroorbital pain, aura, dizziness, or tinnitus.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAt this point, the patient visited an RMP who prescribed her \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Eparacetamol\u003C\/span\u003E for the following symptoms which she consumed three times a day, it provided her with a few intervals of normal body temperature.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was asked to get tested for dengue, the reports were positive for NS1 antigen, hence she came to our outpatient department.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003EOn day 1 of admission (three days ago)\u003C\/span\u003E, the patient developed \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003E6 episodes of vomiting\u003C\/span\u003E within 12 hours duration. The vomitus was non-projectile, non bile stained. There was absence of blood in the vomitus. There were no aggravated or relieving factors. The vomiting was not associated with neck rigidity, or chest or abdominal pain.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient also had f\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #fff2cc;\"\u003Eour episodes of loose stool\u003C\/span\u003E which were non-mucoid, non-blood stained. It was not associated with abdominal pain or tennismus.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn admission, Hess test of a 34 year old male "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is the case of a 34 year old male , autodeiver by occupation , resident of West Bengal who presented to the hospital with chief complaints of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- pus coming out from behind the upper left last molar since 1 month\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHistory of Presenting Illness\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 1 and a half\u0026nbsp; year ago when he developed pain in the left jaw . The pain was sudden onset , continuous , dull aching in character, present at the point in the upper left jaw behind the last molar. The patient describes the pain with heaviness of the jaw. The patient visited a doctor who prescribed him pain killers. The pain subsided but reappeared after 1 week of using medication.\u0026nbsp; No history of trauma\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn the next month , the patient experienced bursting of a swelling in the mouth in the left upper jaw behind the last molar. This resolved the pain completely.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere was a sudden onset of pus discharged from behind that point . The pus was yellow in color, thick in consistency,serous, appreaded every 1- 2 hours on its own, and also appeared when the patient touched his tongue to the site. The pus was not blood stained.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient visited our hospital and was reffered to the dental department where he underwent surgery.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFor 1 year the patient had no symptoms,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAt present , the patient has a reappearance of pus discharge from the same site with same characteristics. The patient also complains of hearing loss in the left ear, which was insidious in onset, gradually progressive. The patient has difficulty hearing in left ear since 1 year .\u0026nbsp; There is absence of tinnitus, aural fullness, pain or discharge from the ear.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFor the past 1 month, the patient has had a rise in blood sugars which were detected but no treatment was taken .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPast History\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient has a left eye corneal opacity since childhood.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESince then the patient has hazy vision in the left eye.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere is history of dental surgery\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot a known case of hypertension , TB , Epilepsy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFamily history\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo similar complaints in the family.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPersonal History\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiet : Mixed\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAppetite : Normal\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBowel and bladder movements: Normal\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESleep adequate\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAddictions :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOccasional consumption\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eof alcohol. Stopped in 2013.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of smoking from 2008 to 2013 - 3 to 4 cigarettes a day .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChewing of tobacco from 2010 to 2021\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3 to 4 a day .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPrevious reports and of a 60 year old male "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EThis is the case of a 60-year-old male, a labourer by occupation who presented to the hospital yesterday afternoon with chief complaints\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Lower back pain since 4 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Chest pain since 4 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Shortness of breath since 4 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHistory of Presenting Illness\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 6 months ago\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6 Months ago the patient developed pain in the left side of the chest which radiated to the left nape of the neck.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt this time, the patient visited 3-4 hospitals, but the pain did not reduce, later on the patient was diagnosed to having an MI after the completion of a few tests at another hospital. The patient underwent angioplasty. After 4 days of the surgery, the patient went for a checkup which was concluded normal.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4 days ago, the patient got drenched in the rain and developed a respiratory tract infection. It lasted for a day. Which led to him experiencing shortness of breath.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe shortness of breath was insidious in onset, non-progressive. It was aggravating due to sputum (yellowish white in color). There was presence of cough The cough was more at night. Thesputum and shortness of brethe were aggravating at night while sleeping. The cough led to vomiting.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe contents of the vomitus was water and sputum . There were 4 - 5 episodes, while going to the hospital in the car.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient also complains of chest pain and lower back pain since then.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe chest pain was insidious in onset, maintaining the same intensity and was described as muscular pain by the patient. It was localised to the left side without any radiation. Lasted till the patient presented to our hospital. There were no aggravating or reliveing factors.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe lower back pain is bilateral , pricking type of pain, insidious in onset, continuous, aggravated by change of positions , walking and lying supine on the bed. It was relived on sleeping on one side(any). It was not radiating .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn reaching another hospital (4 days ago) the patient was given oxygen therapy and nebulisation and given some medication afterwhich the vomiting and shortness of breath stopped.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient also complained of green urine with burning micturition with white discharge for one day , with normal frequency of urination , with no blood or suprapubic pain . He was given medication and it was resolved.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient also complains of itching and\u0026nbsp; skin eruptions bilaterally in the lower limbs since 2 years\u0026nbsp; without any redness.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca
